label: rem:toffoli-q-and
title: The q-AND as a Toffoli gate at the Planck scale
html:
The polynomial P_{7,6}(q) defines the q-AND: the q-deformed AND gate realized by braiding. In the classical Toffoli gate (CCNOT), the target bit flips if and only if both control bits are 1. The 3-strand nuclear braid replaces this Boolean AND with a topological amplitude: two control particles braid around the target to flip its phase.

Three Planck steps. The 3-strand Toffoli braid contains \binom{3}{2} = 3 crossings. A single crossing is not a complete topological operation; one must close the full braid loop. The complete Toffoli gate therefore executes in exactly 3 Planck steps, allocating one step per crossing.

Epoch q t_P(q) Toffoli (3 steps) P_{7,6}
Big Bang \to \infty \to 1 3 units \to -\infty
Physical q_0 10.11 30.3 units -0.1438
Classical \to 1 \to \infty \infty 0

At the Big Bang, each Planck step equals one unit of time and the Toffoli gate executes in the shortest possible time. Near the classical limit the Planck step diverges and the gate freezes: braiding ceases to operate, and the q-AND amplitude vanishes as (q - 1) \to 0.

Factor anatomy. In the canonical convention z_D = q^3/(q^2+1),

  P_{7,6}(q) = -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6} + q^{4} + 2q^{2} + 1\bigr)}{2q\,(q^{2}+1)^{2}} .

The factor (q - 1) measures the departure from classicality: the q-AND magnitude is proportional to the quantum deformation, and vanishes with it. The sextic q^{6} + q^{4} + 2q^{2} + 1 has no positive real root, and neither does (q+1) for q > 0. The q-AND therefore has a single sign change on q > 0, at q = 1, carried entirely by (q-1): it is negative throughout the quantum regime q > 1, and in particular at the substrate anchor.

Orientation. P_{6,7} and P_{7,6} are the forward and reverse Toffoli transitions. They are not related by a sign: taken each from its own input column, P_{6,7}(q_0) = +0.1572 against P_{7,6}(q_0) = -0.1438. Creating a proton from a neutron and annihilating one are distinct amplitudes, not a signed pair.

Universality. The Toffoli gate is universal for reversible classical computation. Any irreversible Turing machine can be simulated by a reversible one relying entirely on Toffoli gates, with at most polynomial overhead in time and space. Combined with a single-qubit gate outside the Clifford group, the Toffoli gate achieves quantum computational universality. Since P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 for every q \neq 1, the substrate's braiding dynamics, operating in discrete Planck steps, is computationally universal away from the classical limit.
